title: A Dynamics for Discrete Quantum Gravity
version: arXiv:1303.0433v1 [gr-qc], submitted 2013-03-02; no journal publication status established in this pass.
section_locator: Abstract and arXiv HTML lines 31-40 (opening summary): classical sequential growth histories are paths through a chain of finite causets; classical law is a Markov chain on a path-space probability space; quantization defines a Hilbert space on paths.
assumptions: Causal-set classical sequential growth process with stepwise transition probabilities; path-space sigma algebra generated by cylinder sets and its induced probability measure. Abstract/summary only; mathematical construction not audited.
conclusion: Author states that the completed universe is represented by a path through the discretely growing chain, with the classical process a Markov chain on path space, and constructs a quantum sequential growth process on a Hilbert space of paths. This explicitly supplies a growth-to-completed-path representation; it does not compare observer-accessible records under competing temporal ontologies.
proof_status: Not verified; discovery lead screened at abstract and opening-summary depth only.
dependencies: Rideout-Sorkin classical sequential growth probabilities; cited by the author, not re-audited in this source
open_questions: Does the detailed QSGP construction define any operationally accessible records that distinguish path order from completed-history representation? Not determined from the screened material.
relevance: Direct predecessor for representing sequential causal-set growth as a completed path-space history, including a quantum extension.
limits: Only abstract/opening summary checked. Do not infer a theorem about ontological equivalence, observer records, or all sequential-growth models.

title: The Objective Past of a Quantum Universe—Part 1: Redundant Records of Consistent Histories
version: arXiv:1312.0331v2 (20 Dec 2013). Journal-publication metadata was not used or independently verified in this lane.
section_locator: Abstract and selected introduction paragraphs on records and observer accessibility (arXiv HTML v2, lines 35-57); no later sections read.
assumptions: Consistent histories for an evolving closed quantum system; redundant consistency imposed through a partial-trace condition; authors distinguish formal global records from records accessible to realistic observers and motivate redundancy across subsystems.
conclusion: Authors propose redundancy of records as a criterion to reduce the consistent-histories set-selection problem. In the introduction they note that a formal record may be a global observable inaccessible to realistic observers, motivating a stronger record principle. The paper does not compare growing-history and completed-history descriptions.
proof_status: Abstract and selected introduction paragraphs screened; no conditions or derivations audited.
dependencies: Consistent histories; decoherence; quantum Darwinism; Finkelstein partial-trace condition, as cited by authors
open_questions: Does this record criterion transfer to sequential causal-set growth, and what record-access algebra would be required? Not answered at this read depth.
relevance: Nearest records-based predecessor identified for explicit discussion of the gap between formal records and realistic observer access.
limits: No growth-versus-block comparison; no claim about temporal ontology or passage. The full technical conditions were not audited.
